title: QUIC server first-flight x25519 key-share compatibility verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home tests with captured quic-go positive proof and deterministic negative coverage for malformed, duplicate, and unadvertised x25519 key shares, followed by SpecTrace, build, full-suite, and diff validation.
scope: Verify that the server accepts an advertised usable first-flight x25519 ClientHello key share without HelloRetryRequest, constructs an x25519 ServerHello and Handshake key material, ignores unsupported hybrid entries, and keeps malformed, duplicate, unadvertised, and fallback HRR behavior bounded.
preconditions: The peer ClientHello is otherwise within the managed TLS 1.3 server subset.
The peer advertises x25519 in supported_groups for x25519 acceptance.
The repo-local RFC 7748 x25519 helper is available for server x25519 derivation.
procedure: Run the focused REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 and REQ-QUIC-CRT-0147 requirement-home tests.
Confirm the captured quic-go first ClientHello with hybrid plus x25519 key shares accepts x25519 without emitting HelloRetryRequest.
Confirm the repo-local x25519 helper matches the RFC 7748 Diffie-Hellman test vector.
Confirm the server publishes Initial ServerHello CRYPTO data selecting x25519 and publishes Handshake packet-protection material.
Confirm malformed, duplicate, and unadvertised x25519 key shares fail deterministically.
Confirm the secp256r1 HelloRetryRequest fallback remains available when no usable first-flight supported share exists and secp256r1 was advertised.
Run SpecTrace core validation, Release build, full Release tests, and diff whitespace checks.
expected_result: Advertised usable first-flight x25519 is accepted without HelloRetryRequest and reaches the existing server Handshake key-publication floor. Unsupported hybrid groups are not selected. Malformed, duplicate, and unadvertised x25519 key shares fail closed. The secp256r1 HRR fallback remains bounded. Public API, IsSupported, HTTP/3, anti-replay, and interop support classification remain unchanged.

supplemental_sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
supplemental_sections.content:
- Captured quic-go first-flight ClientHello selects x25519 without HRR.
- The repo-local x25519 helper matches the RFC 7748 Diffie-Hellman test vector.
- x25519 ServerHello CRYPTO data and Handshake key material are published.
- Malformed, duplicate, and unadvertised x25519 key shares fail closed.
- secp256r1 HRR fallback remains available for eligible first ClientHello attempts without a usable supported key share.
- Public API, IsSupported, HTTP/3, and interop classification remain unchanged.

status_summary: Passed locally for the bounded server first-flight x25519 compatibility slice. The focused filter `FullyQualifiedName~REQ_QUIC_CRT_0154|FullyQualifiedName~REQ_QUIC_CRT_0147|FullyQualifiedName~REQ_QUIC_CRT_0112` passed 32/32 on 2026-05-09 after the cross-platform RFC 7748 helper follow-up, the surrounding CRT regression filter passed 79/79 after preserving legacy P-256 ClientHello fixture behavior, SpecTrace core validated 535 JSON artifacts, `dotnet build Incursa.Quic.slnx -c Release` passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, `dotnet test Incursa.Quic.slnx -c Release --no-build -m:1` passed 4900/4900, and `git diff --check` exited 0. The hosted CI run for commit bbfde64d exposed that Ubuntu does not support `ECDiffieHellman.Create(curve25519)`, so the follow-up replaced that platform dependency with a repo-local RFC 7748 helper and added the RFC 7748 Diffie-Hellman vector to REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 coverage. Public API, IsSupported, HTTP/3, anti-replay, hybrid groups, general group negotiation, and interop zerortt promotion remain out of scope until separate proof.
